chosenSubject: A royal wedding plants the seed for Oktoberfest
chosenAngle: How a wedding celebration for Ludwig and Therese became a public tradition that Munich still remembers
episodeThesis: A community celebration can become history when people repeat it, reshape it, and attach it to a place.
timeline: October 12, 1810: Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria marries Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen
October 17, 1810: Official wedding festivities end with a public horse race on a meadow outside Munich
1811: The Bavarian Agricultural Association helps continue the festival as a yearly event
1819: Munich's city leaders take over organization of the Oktoberfest
1872: Oktoberfest is moved earlier into September to take advantage of milder weather
storyBeats: A child in Munich hears that a royal wedding is not only for palaces: ordinary people are invited to celebrate too
The party moves to a meadow outside the city, where a horse race turns a wedding into a public memory
The meadow receives a name connected to Princess Therese, and the place itself becomes part of the story
Each repeat celebration adds new layers until a one-time wedding party becomes a city tradition
modernRelevance: Modern festivals, school traditions, parades, and annual community events often begin the same way: one shared moment works so well that people decide to bring it back.

sources.title: Muenchen.de: The History of the Oktoberfest in Munich
